DANIEL OKAFOR-REYES
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [GITHUB]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend Engineer with 7 years of experience building backend services in Java and Kotlin, including Spring Boot microservices, REST APIs, and event-driven systems. Experienced with PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing, Kubernetes (EKS), AWS service use, and production on-call. Interested in bringing this production backend experience to a Python-focused role; Python experience to date is scripting rather than production services.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java, Kotlin; Python (scripts for data fixes and small Jenkins helpers); Go (learning; side-project CLI)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, REST APIs, OpenAPI 3
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and containers: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Kubernetes (EKS), Docker; Terraform (read-only familiarity)
Testing and operations: Testcontainers, Spring Cloud Contract, on-call, production incident response

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | 2022-Present
- Build backend microservices with Java/Kotlin and Spring Boot; work with Kafka, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, and AWS services.
- Designed a versioned REST API in OpenAPI 3 for insurance brokers; onboarded 12 partners, serving around 400,000 quote requests per month.
- Implemented a transactional outbox and idempotency keys for Kafka consumers, reducing duplicate claims from around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
- Built an internal Kotlin/Spring Boot service to render policy PDFs from templates; wrote the team's Kotlin coding guidelines.
- Participate in a one-week-per-month on-call rota; handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and wrote an incident account that was praised.
- Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks, since 2024.

Software Developer | Viajar Online | 2019-2021
- Worked on the booking and payments parts of a large Java application.
- Increased payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer refactoring.
- Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Java 11/Spring Boot service using RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf.

SELECTED PROJECT
OpenAPI Spec Diff CLI (Go) | Side project
- Building a learning project that diffs OpenAPI specifications; approximately 600 lines and available on GitHub.

CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional Java SE 11 Developer | 2020
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on Tessel Cargo Software's Routing & Tracking team. I bring seven years of backend development in Java and Kotlin, with hands-on experience building REST services and Kafka-driven systems where reliability and correctness matter. The challenge of turning high-volume carrier events into a dependable live shipment picture is closely aligned with the production problems I have worked on.

At Tejo Insurance Tech, I designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 quoting API now used by 12 broker partners for around 400,000 requests per month. I also addressed duplicate claim creation from at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox and idempotency keys; duplicates fell from around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. These projects involved PostgreSQL, Kubernetes on EKS, and AWS services, and have given me practical experience with event-driven systems, API design, and operating backend services.

My production service experience is in Java and Kotlin, and I am interested in moving into a Python-focused role. My Python experience so far is scripting for data fixes and small Jenkins helpers, rather than shipped services. I would bring proven backend fundamentals, automated testing experience (including Testcontainers and Spring Cloud Contract), and regular on-call incident response. At Tejo I handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and wrote an incident account that was praised.

Tessel's focus on live tracking, Kafka event streams, and engineers who own what they run makes this role especially compelling. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my API, event-processing, and reliability experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
